_comment: The /studio/design op vocabulary: the wire contract between the edit_design
MCP tool (pocketpaw, server pocketpaw_craft) and the layout editor's op
applier (paw-enterprise). Page layout for print: cards, flyers, letterheads.
Committed BYTE-IDENTICAL in both repos:
pocketpaw/ee/pocketpaw_ee/agent/mcp_servers/design_ops.contract.json
paw-enterprise/src/lib/core/studio/craft/contracts/design_ops.contract.json
Shape and rules are the vector contract's (see vector_ops.contract.json),
plus: index (whole number >= 0), int1 (whole number >= 1) and `oneOf`: a
list of param groups; exactly one group must be complete and no param of
another group may appear. ids/id name frames from the page's projection.
`engine` names the designcraft command(s) the applier runs.
UNITS: every position and size is MILLIMETRES measured from the TRIM
top-left of the page (`page`, 0-based; omitted = the page in view), y down.
Bleed is mm. strokeWidth and text size are points (the print convention).
The applier converts: pt = mm x 72 / 25.4, and spread coords = the page's
spread origin + pt. designcraft's object.color reads each CMYK channel <= 1
as a fraction, so the applier passes the 0..1 paint values unchanged (x100
would turn 1% into 1, read as 100%). designcraft runs an `ids` command only
while something is selected, so ops naming ids select them first. type.char's
fill takes only an existing swatch NAME: a text colour that is not a swatch
yet is added with swatch.create first (whole CMYK percents).
Paint: as vector: {c,m,y,k} 0..1 (preferred), "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b]
0..1, {gray} 0..1 or {swatch: name}.
Text colour is set_text_color (or set_text's color): type.char fill on the
frame's story. set_paint paints the frame's BOX (background fill, border),
never the text, so "make the name red" is set_text_color, not set_paint.
Overset: after each batch the applier checks document.inspect's stories and
reports every overset text frame (text cut off, so invisible on the page) in
last_edit.failures as exactly:
overset frame <id>: text does not fit its <w> x <h> mm box at <size> pt; hidden: "<text>"
<w>, <h>, <size> rounded to 0.1 with a trailing .0 dropped; <text> is the
story's first 40 characters. The agent reads it on the next send.
runCommand is the escape hatch, with the same stricter block as photo.

new_document.engine: file.close, then file.new {width, height (pt; size from the presets A4 210x297, A5 148x210, A3 297x420, card 90x54, dl 99x210 mm, Letter 612x792 pt), bleed (pt, default 3 mm), pages, facingPages: false, margins: 12.7 mm}

add_text_frame.engine: frame.create {spread, rect: [x0,y0,x1,y1] spread pt, content: "text", text}, text.exitToFrame (frame.create leaves a caret), then type.char {attrs: {fontFamily: font, size, fill: swatch name of color}}, type.para {attrs: {align (justify -> leftJustified)}}

add_shape.engine: frame.create {spread, rect, shape: rectangle|ellipse, content: "unassigned"} or line.create {spread, a: [x1,y1], b: [x2,y2]}, then object.color / object.fill / object.stroke as set_paint

set_text.engine: story.setText {story of frame id, text}; selection.set {ids: [id]}, type.char {attrs: {fontFamily: font, size, fill: swatch name of color}}, type.para {attrs: {align (justify -> leftJustified)}}; fit: true -> then, while document.inspect lists the frame's story as overset, transform.set {height: current + 0.15 x size pt, ref: 0, ids: [id]} (at most 120 steps; the frame grows DOWN, its top-left stays; the engine's own autoSize is stored but not applied)

set_text_color.engine: per id: selection.set {ids: [id]}, type.char {attrs: {fill: swatch name of color}} (the same path as set_text's color: the glyphs of the frame's whole story)

set_paint.engine: the frame's BOX (background fill, border), never the text: selection.set {ids}; object.color {color (CMYK 0..1 as sent, [r,g,b] x 255, gray g -> K g), target: fill|stroke, ids}; "none" -> object.fill|object.stroke {swatch: "[None]", ids}; {swatch} -> object.fill|object.stroke {swatch, ids}; strokeWidth -> object.stroke {weight, ids}

transform.engine: selection.set {ids}; transform.move {dx, dy (pt), ids}; transform.rotate {angle, ids}; transform.scale {sx: scale / 100, sy: scale / 100, ids} (factors); transform.set {width, height (pt, the visible box: stroke included), ref: 0}

align.engine: selection.set {ids}, object.align {edge: left|hcenter|right|top|vcenter|bottom (center -> hcenter, middle -> vcenter), to, ids}
